summary: NVDA trades at $166.08, about 32% below its 52-week high of $243.37 after an AI-chip sell-off that began in October and deepened on Nov 5 (-9%, no company-specific news reported). Fundamentals are still very strong: Q2 FY27 revenue was $96.2B (+106% y/y) at a 75% gross margin, and the Q3 guide is $108B. At roughly 19x annualised Q2 non-GAAP EPS, the stock sits below our $180-$240 fair range. Conviction is only Medium because earnings land on Nov 17 (3 days away), implied vol is ~60% (99th percentile for the year), gross margin is guided down, and China and custom-silicon share losses are real.

valuation.method: Three-way triangulation. (a) Peers: forward P/E ~24-26x NVDA vs ~30-32x AVGO and 80x+ AMD (secondary aggregators, undated, differing price dates). (b) Earnings power: Q2 non-GAAP EPS $2.22 x4 = $8.88 run-rate; 20x/23x/27x gives $178/$204/$240; assumes no further margin loss beyond guide and revenue flat-to-up from Q2's level (Q3 guide is +12% q/q), ignores FY28 growth upside. (c) Street: consensus target ~$319-327 (Nov 6-9), which is a high anchor and likely stale after the sell-off. Fair range set at $180 / $205 / $240, well below the Street.
valuation.note: Peer P/E (TTM), EV/Sales, growth and operating margin were not obtainable from sources read, so those cells are null rather than guessed. Peer multiples conflict across sources and are unreliable as a precise anchor.
